agent.description: Hand a task to the user's own LLM (the active profile of the axross GUI): it works with the read-only tools inside the MCP root and answers; it can change nothing.

archive.description: List an archive's members; extract it into a fresh folder (mutating).

core.description: File tools of the configured backend; always on, read-only.

crypto.description: Encrypt a file into the axross .axenc format and decrypt it again (mutating).

duplicates.description: Duplicate Finder: scan a folder into the duplicate index, list scans and duplicate groups; dedupe to the axross trash (mutating, dry run by default).

exec.description: Run commands and scripts on remote hosts over SSH, SCP, Telnet, rsh, ADB, WinRM (PowerShell) and Cisco (show commands only); only with --mcp-allow-exec (mutating), refused in the paranoid security mode and on production profiles.

extensions.description: List installed extensions and whether they are enabled (read-only: extensions are GUI plugins).

filetype.description: Identify files by content (magic bytes), flag extension mismatches.

index.description: Build or refresh the offline metadata index that the search tool reads.

metadata.description: Show and export file metadata (EXIF/XMP/IPTC, Office, PDF, media tags); remove it (mutating, writes a cleaned copy).

packer.description: List archive formats; pack files and folders into zip / tar.* / 7z / single-file compression, 7z optionally AES-256 encrypted (mutating).

remote.description: List saved connection profiles (no secrets), open one as an extra backend that every tool can address with its backend argument, close it again.

scripts.description: Saved-script tools; only with --mcp-allow-scripts, stdio only, not confined to the MCP root; refused in the paranoid security mode.

transfer.description: Copy or move files and folders between backends, optionally resumable (mutating).

write.description: Write tools; only with --mcp-write, which needs --mcp-root.

tools.description: List entries in a directory on the configured backend.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: list_dir

tools.description: Return name, type, size, and mtime for one path.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: stat

tools.description: Read up to max_bytes (default 4 MiB) from a file. Returns {content_b64, size, truncated} - or with encoding='text' {text, size, truncated, replaced}: UTF-8, undecodable bytes replaced (replaced=true). truncated=true when the file exceeds the cap.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

encoding.description: base64 (exact bytes) or text (UTF-8, for text files).

tools.name: read_file

tools.description: Content hash of a file. Tries the backend's native fingerprint first (S3 ETag, Drive md5Checksum, ssh sha256sum, etc.); falls back to streaming the file through hashlib when the backend has no cheap hash. The streaming fallback emits MCP progress notifications every few MiB when the caller supplied _meta.progressToken, and stops within one chunk of a notifications/cancelled. algorithm must be one of sha256 / sha1 / md5 / sha512 — backend-specific hash names (etag, dropbox, quickxor) are rejected.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: checksum

tools.description: Search the offline metadata index by name substring, extension, and size range. Free of network round-trips.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: search

tools.description: Breadth-first recursive listing under path. Caps at max_depth (default 4) and max_entries (default 1000). Returns {entries: [{path, name, is_dir, size}], truncated, unreadable: [{path, error}], complete}: unreadable names every folder below path that could not be listed; complete is true only when nothing was cut or left out. An unreadable path itself is an error. Emits MCP progress notifications when the caller supplied _meta.progressToken.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: walk

tools.description: Hash every file under path breadth-first. Each record is either {path, size, algorithm, checksum, source} (hashed), {path, size, algorithm, skipped: "too-large"} (file above max_file_bytes), or {path, size, algorithm, error: "<msg>"} (backend refused that one file), or {path, folder: true, algorithm, error} (a folder that could not be listed: the files below it are missing). complete is true only when every file was hashed and nothing was cut; an unreadable path itself is an error. Emits one progress notification per hashed file; a notifications/cancelled lands within one chunk of the current file. algorithm is one of sha256 / sha1 / md5 / sha512. Defaults: max_files=500, max_depth=10, max_file_bytes=1 GiB. If path names a file instead of a directory the result contains exactly one record.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: recursive_checksum

tools.description: Render a thumbnail of an image file. Returns MCP image content (base64 + mimeType). edge (default 256) is clamped to [16, 2048]. MIME allow-list + size/dimension caps from core.previews apply. Local backends only.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: preview

tools.description: Regex search inside file contents under a root path. Recurses up to max_depth (default 2); skips files larger than 4 MiB. Returns {matches: up to max_matches (default 100, ceiling 500) {path, line_no, line}, files_scanned, truncated, unreadable: [{path, error}] (folders and files that could not be read), complete}. No match with complete=false is no answer. An unreadable path itself is an error. Cooperates with notifications/cancelled.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: grep

tools.description: List historical versions of a file (S3 ObjectVersions, Dropbox revisions, GDrive revision-history, Azure blob snapshots, WebDAV DeltaV, Git: one per commit that changed the file). Empty list on backends with no native versioning.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: list_versions

tools.description: Read a specific historical version of a file. Same max_bytes cap (default 4 MiB) as read_file. version_id comes from list_versions.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: open_version_read

tools.description: Overwrite a file with content (UTF-8 text) or content_b64 (base64 bytes) - exactly one of them. Returns {size}.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

content.description: The new content as UTF-8 text.

content_b64.description: The new content as base64 bytes.

tools.name: write_file

tools.description: Create a directory on the backend.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: mkdir

tools.description: Delete a file or directory.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: remove

tools.description: Move/rename a file or directory. Both src and dst must live under the configured root.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: rename

tools.description: Server-side copy of src to dst. Uses the backend's native copy primitive (S3 CopyObject, WebDAV COPY, shell cp) where available — no client-side streaming.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: copy

tools.description: Copy a file OR directory tree from src into dst. Per-file records: {src, dst, size, action} where action is "copied", "skipped" (reason: "too-large", "exists", "unsafe-name", or "max-depth" for a folder below max_depth), or "error" (folder: true for a folder that could not be listed). "truncated" is true when max_files or max_depth cut the walk; "complete" is true only when every file was copied or already existed. Emits one progress notification per copied file; a notifications/cancelled stops within one file. Defaults: max_files=1000, max_depth=10, max_file_bytes=10 GiB, overwrite=false. Missing dst parent directories are created automatically. Same-backend only in V1 — cross-backend copy is handled by the transfer manager, not the MCP surface.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: bulk_copy

tools.description: Create a symbolic link. target may point anywhere the backend permits (dangling links are allowed); link_path is capped to the MCP root. Raises on backends without symlink support (S3, cloud stores).

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: symlink

tools.description: Create a hard link (second name for the same inode). Cross-device errors surface as the backend's OSError. Most protocols refuse — POSIX/SSH only.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: hardlink

tools.description: Change POSIX mode bits. Accepts integer (420 for 0o644) or octal-string ("0o644" / "644"). Backends without POSIX bits (S3, WebDAV, etc.) raise.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: chmod

tools.description: Names of every saved Python script in the server's script directory (~/.config/axross/scripts/).
tools.name: script_list

tools.description: Describe the ``axross`` scripting API that script_run gives a script, as JSON built from the live code: rules and errors (the conventions and exceptions a script meets), groups (the names by topic), per public function its signature, parameters with types and defaults, return type, whole docstring, examples, ``raises``, ``mutates`` (can change files, remote state or settings) and ``prompts`` (needs a human: under script_run it raises NonInteractiveError unless the script opts in, e.g. confirm(assume_yes=True)); the public classes; the types the API returns (FileItem, results) with fields and methods; the methods every backend session has (with close() and the with statement); and a legend of every field. Same data as axross.api_schema(names) and docs/scripting-api.json. The whole API is large: call it with names=[] for the index, then with the names you need.

names.description: Only these functions, classes and types, plus the types they use; [] gives the index alone. Default: everything.

tools.name: script_api_schema

tools.description: Read the source of a saved script by name. Names are [A-Za-z0-9_-]+; the path is built relative to the server's script directory.
tools.name: script_read

tools.description: Save Python source as ``<name>.py`` (mode 0600) in the server's script directory. Overwrites any existing script with the same name.
tools.name: script_write

tools.description: Remove a saved script by name. Idempotent — no error when the file is already gone.
tools.name: script_delete

tools.description: Run a saved script in its own Python process with ``axross`` (the scripting API; see script_api_schema) in its namespace. stdin is empty, so input() gets EOF and axross.confirm() raises NonInteractiveError unless the script passes assume_yes=True. ``args`` become sys.argv[1:]. The run is stopped after ``timeout_s`` seconds, with every process it started. Returns {name, exit, timed_out, duration_ms, stdout, stderr, namespace_keys} and, after an uncaught exception, error_type, error and traceback; exit follows SystemExit (None is 0, an int is itself, anything else is printed and gives 1) and is the negative signal number of a stopped run. stdout and stderr hold up to 1048576 characters each; more stops the run and fails the call.
tools.name: script_run

tools.description: Read the metadata of a file or of every supported file in a folder: images (JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/TIFF), Office (docx/xlsx/pptx/odt/ods/odp), PDF, audio/video (ffprobe). Returns {path, is_dir, truncated, files: [{path, name, kind, size, error, truncated, removable_count, fields: [{group, name, value, removable}]}]}}. An unsupported or unreadable file is a report with error set, not a failure. Values are length-bounded. Local paths are confined to the MCP root.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

max_files.description: For a folder: at most this many files (truncated=true when cut).

path.description: A file, or a folder whose supported files are used.

recursive.description: For a folder: descend into subfolders.

tools.name: metadata_read

tools.description: The metadata_read data of a file or folder as one text in JSON or CSV. Returns {path, format, files, truncated, text}.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

format.description: json: {"files": [...]}; csv: one row per field, formula-safe.

max_files.description: For a folder: at most this many files (truncated=true when cut).

path.description: A file, or a folder whose supported files are used.

recursive.description: For a folder: descend into subfolders.

tools.name: metadata_export

tools.description: Write the metadata_export text of path into the new file out (under the MCP root, mode 0600). An existing file is never overwritten: 'meta.json' becomes 'meta (2).json'. Returns {path (the file written), format, files, truncated, size}.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

format.description: json: {"files": [...]}; csv: one row per field, formula-safe.

max_files.description: For a folder: at most this many files (truncated=true when cut).

path.description: A file, or a folder whose supported files are used.

recursive.description: For a folder: descend into subfolders.

tools.name: metadata_export_file

tools.description: Remove the metadata of a file, or of every supported file in a folder, by writing a cleaned copy next to each ('photo.jpg' -> 'photo.clean.jpg', then 'photo.clean (1).jpg'); the original is never modified and nothing is overwritten. Images keep orientation and colour profile, pixels are not re-encoded. PDF removal needs pypdf, audio/video needs ffmpeg (both blocked in the paranoid security mode). Returns {path, mode: 'copy', truncated, results: [{path, status (cleaned|unchanged|unsupported|error), output, removed, error, note, sha256}]}.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

max_files.description: For a folder: at most this many files (truncated=true when cut).

path.description: A file, or a folder whose supported files are used.

recursive.description: For a folder: descend into subfolders.

tools.name: metadata_remove

tools.description: Hash every file under a folder into the Duplicate Finder's index (the same index the GUI uses), skipping symlinks and the axross trash; files whose size and mtime did not change are not hashed again unless rehash. Returns {scan_id, root, backend_id, algorithm, files_indexed, status}. One progress notification per file; cancellable (rows indexed so far are kept). Run it before duplicates_groups.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

path.description: Folder; default: the MCP root (local backend).

rehash.description: Hash every file even when unchanged.

tools.name: duplicates_scan

tools.description: The scan history of the addressed backend, newest first, limited to scans of folders inside the MCP root: {scans: [{scan_id, root, backend_id, algorithm, started_at, finished_at, files_indexed, files_in_index, duplicate_groups, status (complete|cancelled|failed|running), error}], truncated}.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

tools.name: duplicates_scans

tools.description: Groups of identical files from the index, every copy inside path. Each group is {algorithm, value (hash), size, copies: [{path, size, mtime, scan_id, keep}]} in survivor order: the first copy (keep=true) is the oldest by mtime (ties: shorter, then alphabetically first path) and is what duplicates_dedupe keeps. The index is a record of the last scan; nothing is read from the files. Returns {path, groups, truncated}.

algorithm.description: Only groups hashed with this algorithm; omit for all.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

max_groups.description: Return at most this many groups.

path.description: Folder; default: the MCP root (local backend).

scan_id.description: Only groups with at least one copy from this scan (duplicates_scans); 0 = rows from before scans were recorded.

tools.name: duplicates_groups

tools.description: Keep the first copy of every duplicate group inside path and move the others to the axross trash (restorable; for the local backend the trash is <MCP root>/.axross-trash). A dry run unless dry_run=false: the dry run only returns the plan. A real run re-checks every copy on disk first: a copy that changed since the scan, or a group without another verified copy, is reported in refused and left alone. Returns {path, dry_run, groups, undated_groups, keep, trash, removed, refused: [{path, reason}], failed: [{path, reason}], trash_root}.

algorithm.description: Only groups hashed with this algorithm; omit for all.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

dry_run.description: true: only plan; false: move the planned copies to the trash.

path.description: Folder; default: the MCP root (local backend).

scan_id.description: Only groups with at least one copy from this scan (duplicates_scans); 0 = rows from before scans were recorded.

tools.name: duplicates_dedupe

tools.description: The archive formats pack can write and whether each is usable here: {formats: [{format, label, suffix, single (exactly one file in), encrypts (takes a password), available, reason}], levels}.
tools.name: pack_formats

tools.description: Pack entries of folder into a new archive folder/archive_name + suffix. Folders are packed recursively; symbolic links are skipped and listed in skipped, never followed. The archive is written to a temporary file first and an existing archive is never overwritten: 'bundle.zip' becomes 'bundle (2).zip'. Only 7z takes a password (AES-256; encrypt_names also hides the file list); ZIP and tar refuse one. Single-file formats (gz, bz2, xz, zst) take exactly one file. Returns {path, format, files, folders, bytes_in, bytes_out, skipped, encrypted}. One progress notification per file; cancellable (nothing is left behind).

archive_name.description: Archive file name without directory; the format's suffix is added when missing.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

encrypt_names.description: 7z with password: also encrypt the file list.

folder.description: Folder holding the entries; the archive is created here.

names.description: Names of files or folders directly inside folder (no path separators, no repeats).

password.description: 7z only: encrypt with AES-256. Never logged or returned.

tools.name: pack

tools.description: List an archive's members without extracting anything: {path, total, truncated, entries: [{name, size (uncompressed), compressed, mtime, is_dir}]}. Local backend only.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

max_entries.description: Return at most this many entries.

path.description: Archive file (zip family, tar.*, 7z, rar, gz/bz2/xz/zst) on the local backend.

tools.name: archive_list

tools.description: Extract an archive into a new folder named after it inside dest_dir (default: the archive's folder): 'x.zip' -> 'x', then 'x-1', … - an existing folder is never written into. Zip-slip, absolute paths, links, more than 10,000 entries, more than 1 GiB or a compression ratio above 100 are refused and nothing is left behind. Returns {path (the new folder), files}. Progress per file; cancellable (the partial folder is removed). Local backend only.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

dest_dir.description: Existing folder under the MCP root to extract into.

path.description: Archive file (zip family, tar.*, 7z, rar, gz/bz2/xz/zst) on the local backend.

tools.name: archive_extract

tools.description: Encrypt a file (at most 1 GiB) into the axross encrypted-overlay format next to it: 'a.txt' -> 'a.txt.axenc', then 'a.txt (2).axenc' - nothing is overwritten. The plaintext stays in place, as in the GUI. Returns {path (the .axenc file), size, plaintext_size}.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

passphrase.description: Passphrase (PBKDF2-SHA256, 200,000 iterations, AES-256-GCM). Never logged or returned.

tools.name: encrypt

tools.description: Decrypt an .axenc file into a new file next to it: 'a.txt.axenc' -> 'a.txt', or 'a (2).txt' when that exists (a name without .axenc gets '.decrypted'); mode 0600, nothing is overwritten. A wrong passphrase or a tampered file fails with nothing written. Returns {path (the plaintext file), size}.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

passphrase.description: Passphrase (PBKDF2-SHA256, 200,000 iterations, AES-256-GCM). Never logged or returned.

tools.name: decrypt

tools.description: Walk a folder and record every entry (name, size, type, mtime) in the offline metadata index that the search tool reads - the same index as the GUI's metadata search. Additive; prune=true also drops index rows under the folder whose file no longer exists. Returns {path, backend_id, recursive, indexed, pruned}. One progress notification per entry; cancellable (what was indexed is kept).

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

path.description: Folder; default: the MCP root (local backend).

prune.description: Also drop rows of files under the folder that are gone.

tools.name: index_build

tools.description: Identify one file by its content (magic bytes), not its name, and say whether the extension matches. Returns {path, name, kind (file|directory|special|error|timeout|cancelled), description, mime (from the content), extension, extension_mime (what the name claims), verdict (match|mismatch|unknown), mismatch (bool), size, encoding, line_endings, engine, file_command, bytes_read, error}. Never fails for an unreadable file: kind is then error or timeout with error set.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

max_bytes.description: Read at most this many bytes per file.

use_file_command.description: Also ask file(1) for its description (local files only).

tools.name: file_type

tools.description: Identify every file under a folder (breadth-first, symlinks skipped). Returns {path, files_scanned, truncated, entries: [{path, name, kind (file|directory|special|error|timeout|cancelled), description, mime (from the content), extension, extension_mime (what the name claims), verdict (match|mismatch|unknown), mismatch (bool), size, encoding, line_endings, engine, file_command, bytes_read, error}]}; with mismatches_only only files whose content contradicts their extension are listed. One progress notification per file; honours cancellation.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

max_bytes.description: Read at most this many bytes per file.

max_depth.description: Subfolder levels to descend (0: the folder itself only).

mismatches_only.description: List only files whose content does not match the extension.

use_file_command.description: Also ask file(1) for its description (local files only).

tools.name: file_type_scan

tools.description: Copy a file or a folder tree from one backend to another (or within one). Local paths are confined to the MCP root, remote ones are not. Existing destination files are skipped unless overwrite; symlinks are skipped; missing destination folders are created. resumable=true copies each file in 4 MiB segments with a local manifest: a cancelled or failed run continues where it stopped when called again with the same arguments. Returns {src, dst, copied, truncated, complete, entries: [{src, dst, size, action (copied|skipped|error), reason, bytes, resumed_segments, error, folder}]}. Every part left out has a record: reason exists, too-large, symlink, unsafe-name, outside-root or max-depth (also sets truncated); a folder that could not be listed is an error with folder=true. complete is true only when every file was copied or already existed. Progress per file; cancellable.

dst.description: Destination path on dst_backend (the file, or the folder that becomes the copy of a source folder).

max_file_bytes.description: Skip files above this size (reason too-large).

max_files.description: Copy at most this many files (truncated=true).

resumable.description: Segmented copy that can continue after an interruption.

src_backend.description: Backend id of the source (list_backends); 'local' is the local file system under the MCP root.

tools.name: transfer_copy

tools.description: Move one file to another backend (copy, then delete the source; the copy is removed again if the source cannot be deleted) or within one backend (rename). An existing destination is refused. Returns {src, dst, bytes}.

dst.description: Destination path on dst_backend (the file, or the folder that becomes the copy of a source folder).

src_backend.description: Backend id of the source (list_backends); 'local' is the local file system under the MCP root.

tools.name: transfer_move

tools.description: The saved connection profiles, without any secret: {profiles: [{name, protocol, host, port, username, auth_type, store_password, production, open_as (backend id when opened in this session, else null), openable, reason (why remote_open would refuse, else empty)}]}.
tools.name: remote_profiles

tools.description: Connect a saved profile and register it as backend 'profile:<name>' for this session; every other tool then reaches it with backend='profile:<name>'. Credentials come from the keyring when the profile stores them; a profile that would need a prompt (password not stored, SSH host key not yet trusted, browser sign-in) fails with an error instead. --mcp-root does not apply to remote paths. Writing needs --mcp-write, and a production-flagged profile stays read-only. Returns {backend, profile, protocol, class, production, writable, reused}.
tools.name: remote_open

tools.description: Disconnect a profile opened with remote_open in this session. Returns {backend, closed}.

backend.description: 'profile:<name>'.

tools.name: remote_close

tools.description: Run one command on a remote host (backend = an id from exec_backends) and return {returncode, stdout, stderr, truncated_stdout, truncated_stderr}. A non-zero exit is a result, not an error. Telnet and ADB deliver stderr inside stdout. Cisco: show commands only. WinRM: PowerShell.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

max_output.description: Bytes of stdout kept (stderr: at most 1 MiB); truncated_* tells when output was cut.

stdin.description: Text fed to the command's stdin (not on WinRM/Cisco).

timeout.description: Seconds before the command is given up.

tools.name: remote_exec

tools.description: Run a script on a remote host: POSIX hosts get it on stdin of sh, bash, python3 or perl with args after it; WinRM hosts run it as PowerShell. Same result as remote_exec.

backend.description: Optional backend id. Omit to use the default; call 'list_backends' to enumerate.

interpreter.description: sh by default; powershell on WinRM.

max_output.description: Bytes of stdout kept (stderr: at most 1 MiB); truncated_* tells when output was cut.

timeout.description: Seconds before the command is given up.

tools.name: remote_script

tools.description: List the backends that can run commands: {backend, class, kind} with kind posix-shell, powershell or ios-show. Open more with remote_open.
tools.name: exec_backends

tools.description: Hand a task to the user's own LLM (the active LLM profile of the axross GUI, or 'profile'). It works with axross' read-only tools inside the MCP root - plus the read-only tools of 'groups' - and returns {answer, stopped, calls, profile, model}. It cannot change files or run commands. Use it to keep file content on the user's machine, e.g. to summarise documents with a local model.

groups.description: Extra tool groups the model may use (read-only tools only).

max_steps.description: Most model requests for this task.

profile.description: An LLM profile name; default: the active one.

task.description: What the local model should do, in plain language.

tools.name: agent_run

tools.description: The installed extensions (user and bundled) and their state, read without importing any of them: {allowed (false in the paranoid security mode), runnable_over_mcp (always false), why_not_runnable, extensions: [{id ('user:<name>' or 'bundled:<name>'), name, version, description, author, source, enabled (switched on in Extensions > Manage Extensions), loadable, error, active (loaded by the GUI: enabled, loadable and allowed)}]}. Extensions are GUI plugins with no headless actions, so none can be run here.
tools.name: extensions_list
